files.module_doc:
m2c/tests/link/link_fakes.py -- Patch C04: a fake device server and the
helpers the link tests share.

Why this is a plain module and not a conftest.py: tests/test_doctor.py does
``from conftest import ...``, which resolves by module name, and a second
conftest.py in tests/link would shadow the real one (the same reason
tests/auth/auth_fixtures.py exists).  Each test file imports what it needs
from here; the autouse fixtures below are re-exported with ``import *`` and so
apply only to the link tests.

The fake server
---------------
``FakeServer`` is a real ``websockets`` server on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral
port, so the client under test runs its genuine network code: handshake,
frames, abrupt connection loss, close codes.  Each connection is handled by a
*script* -- an ``async def script(conn)`` -- chosen by connection number, so a
test says exactly what the server does on the first connection, the second,
and so on.  Ready-made scripts:

    fixture_script(lines)   replays one connection of a P00 golden transcript:
                            for every client line it waits for the client's
                            message and compares it (type, run_id, payload;
                            ids and timestamps are not compared); for every
                            server line it sends it verbatim.
    ReplayRun(events)       a tiny model of the server's resume rule
                            (protocol/README.md section 5): it holds a run's
                            w

m2c/tests/link/test_link_golden.py -- Patch C04: replay the P00 golden
transcripts (protocol/fixtures/*.jsonl) against the client.

This is the "client side" of the contract (protocol/README.md section 9): a
fake server plays the server lines of a transcript verbatim and checks every
client line it receives (type, run_id, payload; ids and timestamps are not
compared).  ONE generic driver performs the client's side of any transcript,
so a new golden transcript is covered without new test code:

    run.start        -> link.start_run(**payload)
    user_message     -> link.send_user_message
    tool_result      -> link.send_tool_result, once the tool_proposed it
                        answers has been delivered to the callback
    approval         -> link.send_approval, same wait
    ping             -> link.ping(nonce)
    hello / run.resume are the link's own business and are checked, not driven.

Afterwards the local store must hold exactly the transcript's server stream,
in order, with the server's seq recorded.

m2c/tests/link/test_link_logging.py -- Patch C04: the link never logs message
content, prompts, file contents or the device credential (build plan 11.4, and
the C04 work package).  It logs message types, ids and error codes only.

Attacked from three sides, like C03's redaction test:

* a run with distinctive secret-looking strings in every place content can
  travel (what the user typed, what the model said, a file path and a search
  pattern in a tool call, tool output, instructions, a server error's text) is
  driven through every code path that logs -- connect, kill, resume, gap,
  unknown run, malformed event, rejected request, a store failure, a revoked
  device -- with the RAW log records captured; the records and every rendering
  of every exception are searched for those strings;
* the source is parsed: no ``logger.exception``/``exc_info``/``print``, logging
  calls take a literal or go through ``log_event`` with allowlisted keys, and
  the credential is revealed in exactly one function;
* repr() of the link shows nothing.

m2c/tests/link/test_link_requests.py -- Patch C04: request/response correlation,
the ping/pong keepalive, what the client sends, and sending while not connected.

Correlation in protocol v1: a ``pong`` echoes the ping's ``nonce``; an
``error`` names the message it answers in ``ref_id`` (the message's ``id``);
there is no other reply type.  So the link keeps a table of pending requests
and settles each from one of those two, with a timeout.

files.module_doc:
m2c/tests/link/test_link_resume.py -- Patch C04: reconnect and run.resume, the
"Done when" test of this work package:

    killing the connection mid-stream resumes without duplicate or missing events.

The server side is ``ReplayRun`` (link_fakes.py), which follows the rule of
protocol/README.md section 5: on run.resume{last_seq} re-deliver every event
with seq > last_seq verbatim.  What is checked is the DEVICE LOG, the source of
truth (build plan O1): after however many kills, the stored server events are
exactly seq 1..N once each, in order, and the local sequence has no holes.

Also here: duplicates are ignored by seq, a gap is never stored out of order
(the client asks again from last_seq), last_seq is recovered from the store
after a restart -- including a real SIGKILL of the client process -- and the
details of which runs are resumed and how.

m2c/tests/link/test_link_shutdown.py -- Patch C04: graceful shutdown.

``aclose()`` must close the socket properly, cancel every task the link
started, settle every waiter, and leave the store consistent: nothing
half-written, and the in-memory cursor equal to what the log says.
